comment: File-based allow-list for the retrieval MCP server: one entry per role, naming exactly the retrieval operations that role may call.

The server reads this file at startup and checks it as the first statement of retrieve. A role that is not listed as holding 'retrieve' is refused with an authorization_denied error naming the role, the operation and the roles that ARE allowed, and the refusal is journalled to the same audit log that records the successful calls.
A role that is absent from 'roles' is an unknown role and is refused, as is a missing or blank role; nothing is defaulted to an allowed role.
Derived from docs/routing-and-tool-grant-map.json: every 'mcp__retrieval__retrieve' string under 'grants.<role>' becomes a grant here, and nothing else does.

The classification ceiling is NOT duplicated in this file. The server reads the per-role ceiling from 'retrieval_ceiling' in docs/routing-and-tool-grant-map.json and takes the stricter of that ceiling and the caller's requested ceiling, so one file stays the source of truth for the ceiling.
Written as valid JSON with no comments: the explanation lives in these string fields.
derivation: grants[role] filtered to the operations this server exposes; a role granted 'retrieve' must also carry a retrieval_ceiling above 'none' in the routing map, and the server refuses to start if the two files disagree

denial_note_by_role.orchestrator: refused retrieve: it sequences roles and reads their returns, and queries no corpus
denial_note_by_role.planner: holds retrieve at ceiling internal: a plan is grounded in the project's own reference documents, and nothing above internal is storable in project memory
denial_note_by_role.implementer: holds retrieve at ceiling internal: the implementer grounds code changes in the reference corpus, bounded to internal
denial_note_by_role.tester: refused retrieve: it works from the supplied acceptance criteria and the gate output, and searches no corpus
denial_note_by_role.reviewer: holds retrieve at ceiling internal: a review cites the same reference documents the change cites, bounded to internal
denial_note_by_role.project-manager: refused retrieve: it owns the ticket tool and performs no reference lookup
denial_note_by_role.researcher: refused retrieve: its channel is the open web, and the internal corpus would only widen its context

denial_note_by_operation.retrieve: refused to the roles that read no corpus at all, so no reference document reaches a context that does not need one; the ceiling then bounds the four roles that do, and a role capped at internal can never obtain a confidential or secret document by asking for a higher ceiling
